questions.question: Aruna sells an article at a certain price. Had she sold it at three-fifth of that selling price, she would have lost 20%. What is the gain percentage when she sells it at 90% of the original selling price?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

She lost 20% when she sold it at 3/5 of actual selling price.

**Formula Used:**

Gain/Profit = SP – CP,

Percent gain/Profit = (SP – CP)/CP × 100,

Where,

SP is selling price,

CP is cost price 

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price be Rs. 100

When she sold at 3/5 of actual selling price he lost 20% on CP

⇒ 3/5 × SP = 80% × 100

⇒ 3/5 × SP = 80/100 × 100

⇒ 3/5 × SP = 80

⇒ SP = (80 × 5)/3

⇒ SP = 400/3

Actual selling price is 400/3

Now she sold at 90% of a actual selling price.

⇒ 90/100 × 400/3

⇒ 120

Now gain = SP – CP

⇒ Gain = 120 – 100

⇒ Gain = 20

Gain % = P/CP × 100

⇒ Gain % = 20/100 × 100

⇒ Gain % = 20%

**∴ Total gain percent is 20%.**

questions.question: A fruit merchant makes a profit of 25% by selling mangoes at a certain price. If he charges Rs. 3 more on each mango, he will gain 40%. Find the cost price of one mango
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in profit percentages = 40% − 25% = 15%

This 15% of CP corresponds to the increase in selling price, which is Rs. 3.

⇒ 15% of CP = 3

⇒ 1% of CP = 3 ÷ 15 = 0.2

⇒ 100% of CP = 0.2 × 100 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit in case 1 = 25%

Profit in case 2 = 40%

Difference in Selling Prices (SP₂ − SP₁) = Rs. 3

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/16b55e837fea47bf9fb764c3a36dae58fab694313833894abda91be9ad9d5694.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of one mango be Rs. x.

⇒ SP₁ = x × 125 ÷ 100 = 1.25x

⇒ SP₂ = x × 140 ÷ 100 = 1.40x

According to the question,

⇒ SP₂ − SP₁ = 3

⇒ 1.40x − 1.25x = 3

⇒ 0.15x = 3

⇒ x = 3 ÷ 0.15 = 300 ÷ 15

⇒ x = 20

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always given on the Marked Price (MP) unless specified otherwise. Formula: SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the effective single discount percentage is: a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer sells at CP but uses false weight, Profit % = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.

questions.question: The profit earned on selling an article for Rs. 4550 is 5 times of the loss incurred on selling the same article for Rs. 3290. What will be the selling price of the article to earn a profit of 20 percent?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Profit** to **Loss** is 5 : 1.

Difference in **Selling Prices** = 4550 − 3290 = 1260.

Divide difference by sum of ratio parts (5 + 1 = 6): 1 unit = 1260 ÷ 6 = 210.

**Cost Price (CP)** = Loss SP + 1 unit = 3290 + 210 = 3500.

New **Selling Price (SP)** for 20% profit = 3500 × 120 ÷ 100 = 4200.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 4200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP₁ = Rs. 4550, SP₂ = Rs. 3290, Profit = 5 × Loss, Target Profit = 20%.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Loss = CP − SP | New SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/961a0467072d656acc972b98624919a17ee55079e73f5e676174a1fa7ebe35df.png] 

⇒ Let the loss be x. Then Profit = 5x.

⇒ (4550 − CP) = 5 × (CP − 3290)

⇒ 4550 − CP = 5CP − 16450

⇒ 6CP = 21000 ⇒ **CP = 3500**

⇒ New SP = 3500 × (120 ÷ 100) = 4200.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 4200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price Calculation

When Profit and Loss are related for the same article at different prices, the CP acts as the **central reference point**. CP = (n × SPₗₒₛₛ + SPₚᵣₒfᵢₜ) ÷ (n + 1) where Profit = n × Loss.

Profit Percentage

Profit % is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise. Formula: Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.</p

questions.question: A fabric seller sells 65 m of cloth for Rs. 5,850 at a profit of Rs. 11 per metre of cloth. What is the cost price of 1 m of cloth?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price of 65m of cloth = Rs. 5,850

Profit earned per metre of cloth = Rs. 11

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of 1 metre of cloth be x.

The total cost price of 65 metres of cloth = 65x

The selling price of 65 metres of cloth = 65(x+11) = 65x + 715

According to the given information,

65x + 715 = 5,850

Solving for x, we get:

65x = 5,850 - 715

65x = 5,135

x = 79

**Therefore, the cost price of 1 metre of cloth is Rs. 79.**

questions.question: The cost prices of articles A and B are Rs. 1200 and Rs. 1600 respectively. The selling price of article A is Rs. 1380 and the total profit on selling both the articles is 25%. What is the profit percentage on the selling of article B?
questions.solution:

⇒ The selling price of articles A and B = cost price × (100 + profit)% = 2800 × 125%

⇒ The selling price of articles A and B = Rs. 3500

⇒ The selling price of articles A + the selling price of articles B = 3500

⇒ 1380 + the selling price of articles B = 3500

⇒ The selling price of articles B = Rs. 2120

⇒ Profit % on article B = [(2120 – 1600)/1600] × 100 = 520/16 = 32.5%

questions.question: After selling the article for Rs. 430, a person had a loss of 14%. For earning a gain of 14% how much amount an article will be sold?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price at 14% loss = Rs. 430

Desired profit = 14%

**Concept:**

⇒ Cost Price = Selling price/(1 - loss %/100)

⇒ New Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 + profit %/100)

**Solution:**

⇒ Cost Price = Rs. 430/(1 - 14/100) = Rs. 500

⇒ New Selling Price = Rs. 500 × (1 + 14/100) = Rs. 570

**Therefore, to earn a gain of 14%, the article should be sold for Rs. 570.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper offers a scheme on the purchase of shirts: ‘Buy two, get one free of the same kind’. The cost price of one shirt is ₹300. What should be the selling price (in ₹) of one shirt if he wants to earn 30% profit?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total shirts in transaction = 2 (Paid) + 1 (Free) = 3 shirts.

Total Cost Price (CP) = 3 × ₹300 = ₹900.

Total Selling Price (SP) needed for 30% profit = 900 × 130% = ₹1170.

Since the customer pays for only 2 shirts, the SP of one shirt = ₹1170 ÷ 2 = ₹585.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹585.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

CP of 1 shirt = ₹300

Scheme = Buy 2, Get 1 Free

Desired Profit = 30%

 
 Shirt 1
 CP: ₹300
 
 
 Shirt 2
 CP: ₹300
 
 
 Free Shirt
 CP: ₹300
 
 
• 
 Total Shirts Handed Over = 3
 Total CP = ₹900

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Cost Price for 3 shirts = 3 × 300 = ₹900

⇒ Profit desired = 30% of ₹900 = (30 ÷ 100) × 900 = ₹270

⇒ Total Selling Price required = Total CP + Profit = 900 + 270 = ₹1170

⇒ Number of shirts paid for by the customer = 2

⇒ Selling price of one shirt = Total SP ÷ Number of shirts paid = 1170 ÷ 2

⇒ Selling price of one shirt = ₹585

**∴ The correct answer is ₹585.**

**__Additional Information__**

Discount Percentage in Free Schemes

Discount % = (Number of free items ÷ Total number of items) × 100. For 'Buy 2 Get 1', Discount = (1 ÷ 3) × 100 = 33.33%.

Effective Profit Relation

Total SP = Total CP × (1 + Profit/100). The total SP is then distributed only over the items actually sold (paid for).

Marked Price and Discount

If a discount is offered on Marked Price (MP), then SP = MP × (1 − Discount/100). In 'Buy X Get Y' schemes, MP is often the price of one item.

questions.question: A manufacturer earns a profit of 10% on selling his products to a wholesale dealer. The wholesale dealer earns a profit of 15% by selling it to a retailer. The retailer, in turn, earns a profit of 25% from the customer. What is the actual cost of production of an article for which the customer pays Rs. 12,650?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Customer pays = Rs. 12,650.

Profit to retailer = 25%.

Profit to wholesale dealer = 15%.

Profit to manufacturer = 10%.

**Formula Used:**

Actual cost = Final amount / [(1 + Profit percentage/100)ⁿ], where n is the number of times the profit is applied.

**Calculation:**

Let the cost of production be Rs. x.

⇒ Price after manufacturer's profit = x × (1 + 10/100)

⇒ Price after wholesale dealer's profit = x × (1 + 10/100) × (1 + 15/100)

⇒ Price after retailer's profit = x × (1 + 10/100) × (1 + 15/100) × (1 + 25/100)

⇒ 12,650 = x × (1.1) × (1.15) × (1.25)

⇒ 12,650 = x × 1.1 × 1.15 × 1.25

⇒ x = 12,650 / (1.1 × 1.15 × 1.25)

⇒ x = 12,650 / 1.58125

⇒ x = 8,000

**The actual cost of production of the article is Rs. 8,000.**

questions.question: A person bought an article and sold it at a loss of 10 percent. If he had bought it for 30 percent less price and sold it for Rs. 20 more, then he would earn a profit of 40 percent. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial **Cost Price (CP₁)** be 100 units.

Initial **Selling Price (SP₁)** at 10% loss = 100 − 10 = 90 units.

New **Cost Price (CP₂)** at 30% less = 100 − 30 = 70 units.

New **Selling Price (SP₂)** at 40% profit = 70 + (40% of 70) = 70 + 28 = 98 units.

Difference in SP = 98 − 90 = 8 units → Rs. 20.

8 units = Rs. 20 ⇒ 100 units = (20 ÷ 8) × 100 = Rs. 250.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial loss = 10%, New CP reduction = 30%, New profit = 40%, SP increase = Rs. 20.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cac78889980cc89d2f2c31023b15de6d69f8b73cd16b580fb573f83ec824f73e.png] 

⇒ Let the initial **Cost Price** be x.

⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = 0.90x

⇒ New Cost Price (CP₂) = x − 0.30x = 0.70x

⇒ New Selling Price (SP₂) = 0.70x + 40% of 0.70x

⇒ SP₂ = 0.70x × 1.40 = 0.98x

⇒ Difference in SP = SP₂ − SP₁ = 0.98x − 0.90x = 0.08x

⇒ Given 0.08x = 20

⇒ x = 20 ÷ 0.08 = 2000 ÷ 8 = 250

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Always calculate profit or loss on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise.

Selling Price Formula

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 or SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

Percentage Change

When a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the effective change is [a + b + (ab ÷ 100)]%.</p

questions.question: Veer buys 200 guavas for Rs. 1,800. Some of these guavas are rotten and are thrown away. He sells the remaining guavas at Rs.14 each and makes a profit of Rs. 230. The percentage of guavas thrown away is:

questions.question: A trader sells two shirts for Rs. 4500 each article. If he earns a profit of 20 percent on one and loses 40 percent on the other, then what will be his overall loss percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price of each shirt = Rs. 4500

Profit on the first shirt = 20%

Loss on the second shirt = 40%

**Formula Used:**

Profit or Loss Percentage = (Total Profit or Loss)/(Total Cost Price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the first shirt be C₁ and the cost price of the second shirt be C₂.

For the first shirt:

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 4500

Profit = 20%

Cost Price (CP) = C₁

4500 = C₁ + 0.2C₁

4500 = 1.2C₁

⇒ C₁ = 4500 / 1.2

⇒ C₁ = 3750

For the second shirt:

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 4500

Loss = 40%

Cost Price (CP) = C₂

4500 = C₂ - 0.4C₂

4500 = 0.6C₂

⇒ C₂ = 4500 / 0.6

⇒ C₂ = 7500

Total Cost Price (CP) = C₁ + C₂

Total Cost Price (CP) = 3750 + 7500

Total Cost Price (CP) = 11250

Total Selling Price (SP) = 4500 + 4500

Total Selling Price (SP) = 9000

Total Loss = Total Cost Price - Total Selling Price

Total Loss = 11250 - 9000

Total Loss = 2250

Loss Percentage = (Total Loss) / (Total Cost Price) × 100

Loss Percentage = 2250 / 11250 × 100

Loss Percentage = 20%

**The overall loss percentage is 20%.**

questions.question: The price of an article increases by 20% every year. If the difference between the price of the article at the end of the third year and at the end of the fourth year is Rs. 324, what is the price of the article at the end of the second year ?
questions.solution:
Given:

The price of an article increases by 20% every year. 

The difference between the price of the article at the end of the third year and at the end of the fourth year is Rs. 324.

Concept used:

Compound interest = P(1 + R/100)n - P

where, P = Principal amount, R = Rate of interest per year

N = time in years

Calculation:

Let the initial price of the article be Rs. P.

The price of the article at the end of the fourth year = Rs. P(1 + 20/100)4

The price of the article at the end of the third year = Rs. P(1 + 20/100)3

The price of the article at the end of the second year = Rs. P(1 + 20/100)2

According to the question,

P(1 + 20/100)⁴ - P(1 + 20/100)3 = 324

⇒ P × 1.2⁴ - P × 1.2³ = 324

⇒ P × 1.2³ (1.2 - 1) = 324

⇒ P × 1.728 × 0.2 = 324

⇒ P = 937.5

⇒ P(1 + 20/100)2 = 1350

**∴ Rs. 1350 is the price of the article at the end of the second year.**

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **no profit or loss**, the **Selling Price (SP)** must be equal to the **Cost Price (CP)**.

Let the multiplier for each **equal discount** be 'k'.

k² = **SP** / **MP** = 121.5 / 150 = 81 / 100

k = √(81 / 100) = 9 / 10

**Discount Percentage** = (1 − 9/10) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price (CP)** of the pen = ₹121.5

**Marked Price (MP)** of the pen = ₹150

Condition: **No profit or loss** after two equal **successive discounts**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0637ee0fd18af96cd6fc45307178f9dd444a1cb48872b6acff57158728aa1601.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**SP** = **MP** × (1 − r/100)ⁿ

Where 'r' is the discount rate and 'n' is the number of discounts.

**Calculations:**

⇒ For no profit or loss, **SP** = **CP** = ₹121.5

⇒ 121.5 = 150 × (1 − x/100)²

⇒ (1 − x/100)² = 121.5 / 150

⇒ (1 − x/100)² = 1215 / 1500

⇒ (1 − x/100)² = 81 / 100

⇒ 1 − x/100 = √(81 / 100)

⇒ 1 − x/100 = 9 / 10

⇒ x/100 = 1 − 0.9

⇒ x/100 = 0.1

⇒ x = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

No Profit No Loss Case

This condition occurs when the **Selling Price (SP)** is exactly equal to the **Cost Price (CP)** of the product.

Successive Discounts Formula

If two discounts are 'a%' and 'b%', the **equivalent single discount** is given by: [a + b − (ab/100)]%.

Marked Price (MP) Relation

MP = CP × (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%). If Profit% is zero, then MP/CP = 100 / (100 − Net Discount%).
